S3.01.needs: an AGI account and a browser on the Mac
S3.01.note: The Desktop sign-in is a browser handoff; the web sign-in form is the same email step.
steps: Open the AGI Desktop app while signed out, so the sign-in screen with the line 'Sign in to' and the button Continue in browser shows.
Click Continue in browser.
In the browser that opens, sign in with your AGI account (email, or a provider).
Return to the Desktop app and wait for the handoff to finish.
Look for a signed-in app: the sign-in screen should be gone. Compare with Expected.
S3.01.where: Open AGI Desktop > Continue in browser (sign-in screen). On the web, /login > Log in or sign up

S3.02.needs: a new email address that has no AGI account
S3.02.note: No separate sign-up screen was found; the same email step handles new and existing accounts. The string Create account exists in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/auth.json but I did not find where it is shown.
steps: On the sign-in screen, find the field labelled Email address.
Type an email address that has no AGI account yet.
Click Continue.
Look for the next step (a code or password step) that a new account goes through. Compare with Expected.
S3.02.where: Log in or sign up (sign-in screen) > type a new email > Continue

S3.03.needs: a new email address you can read
S3.03.note: I did not trace which server state sends a new account to this step; the blocked-before-confirm check is not verified in code.
steps: Sign up with a new email address (see S3.02).
On the next screen, read the heading Confirm your email address.
Open the email inbox and find the message with the code.
Enter the code and confirm, then try to use the app before confirming to see that it is blocked.
Compare with Expected: the account is usable only after the email is confirmed.
S3.03.where: Log in or sign up > new email address > Continue > Confirm your email address

S3.04.needs: an account whose email you can read
S3.04.note: The one-time-code autofill attribute was not checked in code.
steps: Enter an email address of an existing account and click Continue.
On the Verify this device screen, check the inbox for the emailed code.
Type the code into the field labelled Code and click Continue.
Click Resend code and watch for the countdown text Resend code in ... seconds.
Compare with Expected: the code is accepted, and resend works after the countdown.
S3.04.where: Log in or sign up > email > Continue > Verify this device (code step)

S3.06.needs: an account with a password and an inbox you can read
S3.06.note: The wording of the message shown after the click was not traced.
steps: Enter the email of an account that has a password, then click Continue.
On the password screen, click Forgot password?.
Check what message appears and whether a reset email arrives.
Compare with Expected: a reset code or link is sent by email.
S3.06.where: Log in or sign up > email > Continue > Forgot password?

S3.07.needs: an account with a password and an inbox you can read
S3.07.note: The heading of the new password screen was not found; the labels above come from the step file.
steps: Start a reset as in S3.06 and open the reset email.
Enter the code on the reset screen and click Continue.
On the new password screen, type a new password and click Continue.
Compare with Expected: you are signed in with the new password.
S3.07.where: Log in or sign up > email > Continue > Forgot password? > emailed code > Continue (new password step)

S3.08.note: Which providers appear depends on configuration in apps/web/features/auth/authProviderConfig.ts, which I did not check.
steps: On the sign-in screen, look under the email field for buttons that start with Continue with.
Click Continue with Google (or Continue with GitHub).
Complete the provider's sign-in in the window that opens.
Compare with Expected: the app signs you in and returns you to it.
S3.08.where: Log in or sign up > Continue with Google (or Continue with GitHub)

S3.09.needs: an account in an organization that uses single sign-on
S3.09.note: No button is named for SSO. The redirect starts from the Continue step when the server reports an enterprise connection (apps/web/features/auth/IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx around line 393).
steps: Enter the work email of an SSO-enabled organization on the Log in or sign up screen.
Click Continue.
Expect to be sent to your organization's sign-in page in the browser; complete it.
Compare with Expected: you land back in the app signed in.
S3.09.where: Log in or sign up > work email > Continue (web). On AGI Desktop: Continue in browser, then sign in with your organization's single sign-on

S3.10.needs: a work email of an organization with single sign-on, and a personal email
S3.10.note: The domain match itself is decided on the server through the sign-in factors; the client only follows the enterprise result. I did not trace the server domain lookup.
steps: On the Log in or sign up screen, type a work email address of an organization that has its own sign-in.
Click Continue.
Compare with Expected: you are routed to that organization's sign-in page instead of a password screen.
Try a personal address on the same screen and compare: it should show the normal password or code step.
S3.10.where: Log in or sign up > type a work email > Continue

S3.11.needs: a signed-in account and a Mac or device that supports passkeys
S3.11.note: The same panel is used on the web settings screen as well as in the Desktop app.
steps: Sign in, then open Settings and click Security.
Scroll to the Passkeys section.
Click Add a passkey and complete the system passkey prompt.
Look for the new passkey in the list, with its own rename and remove controls.
Compare with Expected: the passkey is registered and listed.
S3.11.where: Settings > Security > Passkeys > Add a passkey

labels.text: Sign in with a passkey or security key

S3.12.needs: an account with a registered passkey and a passkey-capable device
S3.12.note: The button only appears when passkey sign-in is configured and the browser supports passkeys (apps/web/features/auth/authProviderConfig.ts and AuthEmailStep.tsx).
steps: Sign out, then open the sign-in screen.
Type the email of the account that has a passkey, or leave it blank if the button is shown without it.
Click Sign in with a passkey or security key.
Pick the passkey in the system prompt.
Compare with Expected: you are signed in without a password or code.
S3.12.where: Log in or sign up > Sign in with a passkey or security key

S3.13.needs: a signed-in account and an authenticator app on a phone
S3.13.note: The screen can say Authenticator apps are temporarily unavailable; the exact QR and setup-key wording was not checked.
steps: Open Settings, click Security, and find the Authenticator app block.
Click Set up authenticator app.
Add the shown key or QR code to an authenticator app on your phone, then type the six-digit code.
Click Enable two-factor to confirm.
Sign out and sign in again: a second-factor step should appear. Compare with Expected.
S3.13.where: Settings > Security > Authenticator app > Set up authenticator app

S3.14.needs: an account with two-factor on and its authenticator app
S3.14.note: Which factor is asked first depends on the account; the other alternatives are text, email and authenticator codes in the same file.
steps: With two-factor on (S3.13), sign out and sign in with the email and password.
Read the Confirm it is you screen and the factor it asks for.
Click Use a backup code to see the alternative, then go back and use the authenticator code.
Compare with Expected: the session starts only after the second factor.
S3.14.where: Log in or sign up > email > Continue > password (or code) > Confirm it is you

labels.text: I have saved these backup codes somewhere safe

S3.15.needs: an account where two-factor is being set up, and an authenticator app
S3.15.note: The path for regenerating codes later was not traced.
steps: Finish the two-factor setup in S3.13 by entering a valid code.
Read the Backup codes list that appears.
Click Copy codes, Download codes or Print codes, and check each result.
Tick I have saved these backup codes somewhere safe and click Done.
Compare with Expected: the codes are shown once and cannot be read again.
S3.15.where: Settings > Security > Authenticator app > Set up authenticator app (codes appear after the code is accepted)

labels.text: Lost the device with your codes?

S3.16.needs: an account you can no longer fully sign in to
S3.16.note: The recovery page at /recover is the same form. The request is handled as a support ticket, and the final submit result was not traced.
steps: On the password screen, click Can’t reach this email?.
Choose what you lost from the list (password, email access, or two-factor device and backup codes).
Fill in the text box to describe what happened and submit.
Compare with Expected: you see a confirmation that the request was sent.
S3.16.where: Log in or sign up > email > Continue > Enter your password > Can’t reach this email? (or Lost the device with your codes? on the Confirm it is you step)

S3.17.needs: an outside account (Google or GitHub) to link
S3.17.note: Rows for sign-in methods also show a Remove button for identities; I did not trace which one unlinks.
steps: Sign in, open Settings, and click Security.
Find the Sign-in methods block.
Click Connect on a provider such as Google, and finish the outside sign-in.
Check that the row now shows the account and a Disconnect button.
Click Disconnect and confirm, then compare with Expected.

S3.18.needs: an existing account and a second email address
S3.18.note: Searched apps/web/features/auth, apps/web/app/login and apps/web/app/signup for already exists, already registered, already linked, no account, not registered, sign in instead and sign up instead; no matching copy was found. The cited lines (AuthEmailStep.tsx:80, IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:301) hold no such message.

S3.19.needs: a new email for sign-up; a re-prompt needs a Terms version change, which you cannot cause from the UI
S3.19.note: The re-prompt on a Terms change is enforced on the server (apps/web/lib/server/terms.ts) and cannot be triggered from the UI.
steps: Sign up with a new email (S3.02) and reach the sign-up terms gate.
Read the line I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
Check that the continue button stays disabled until the box is ticked.
Tick the box and continue.
For a re-prompt, sign in to an account whose terms need review: the Sign out button on the review screen appears. Compare with Expected.
S3.19.where: Log in or sign up > new email > Continue (sign-up gate on /signup shows the I agree to the checkbox)

S3.21.note: The save target of the name was not traced; the Settings > General check is inferred from the settings navigation keywords.
steps: Sign in with a new account so the Welcome setup opens.
Type your name in the Preferred name field.
Click Continue, then pick a role and a first use (S3.23).
Open Settings > General and check that the name shows up.
Compare with Expected: the name is saved to the account.
S3.21.where: Sign in as a new account > Welcome screen (/welcome) > Preferred name

labels.text: What do you want to do first?

S3.23.note: How the chosen role and use shape replies was not traced past the saved preferences.
steps: On the Welcome screen, type a name and open the What best describes your work? list.
Pick one role, then click Continue.
On What do you want to do first?, pick one option such as Write and debug code.
Read the starter prompts shown for that option, then click Finish.
Compare with Expected: the first chat reflects the chosen use.
S3.23.where: Sign in as a new account > Welcome screen (/welcome) > What best describes your work? > Continue > What do you want to do first?

S3.24.note: The Welcome screen asks only for name, role and first use; personalization style is set in Settings > Personalization, not in onboarding.
steps: Open Settings and click Personalization.
Set Response style, Response length and Technical level.
Send a question in a new chat.
Compare the reply with the chosen style and length.

labels.text: Import memory from other AI providers

S3.26.needs: an account on another assistant to copy memories from
S3.26.note: MemorySection is placed under Personalization was not traced line by line; the path follows the settings screen mapping in WebSettingsModal.tsx.
steps: Open Settings, click Personalization, and find the row Import memory from other AI providers.
Click the import button for that row, then pick a source (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or Other).
Click Copy prompt and paste the prompt into the other assistant; then paste or upload its answer.
Review the preview list, select items, and click Start import.
Compare with Expected: the chosen memories appear in your saved memories.
S3.26.where: Settings > Personalization > Import memory from other AI providers > Start import

S3.27.note: Searched apps/web for recommend (onboarding, connectors, settings, chat); no recommended-app list or guided connector flow was found. WebSettingsModal.tsx lines 309 and 337 only load the Connectors panel through the adapter, with no recommendations.

S3.29.needs: the AGI Desktop app on a Mac
S3.29.note: No Screen Recording guidance text was found; the macOS Accessibility prompt is opened from apps/desktop/electron/runtime/systemPermissions.ts.
steps: In the Desktop app, open Settings and click Computer use.
Read the hint Let AGI see your screen and use the mouse and keyboard in apps you allow.
Look at the Control block with the Any app setting.
Click Manage next to Allowed apps, add an app, and check the list.
When a macOS permission is needed, the Accessibility prompt opens. Compare with Expected: the grants are recorded in the list.
S3.29.where: Settings > Computer use (AGI Desktop app only) > Allowed apps > Manage

S3.30.needs: Chrome with the AGI extension and the AGI Desktop app on a Mac
S3.30.note: The Pair button text on the Desktop side was not found; pairing starts from the Chrome side panel, and the code dialog is opened by Desktop.
steps: Open Settings and click Capabilities, then find the Chrome block.
If it says nothing has asked to pair yet, install the extension in Chrome.
In Chrome, open the Extension side panel, choose Connect to Desktop, and type the code the app shows in its dialog.
Check that the block reads Paired and answering.
Click Unpair and confirm Unpair this browser?, then compare with Expected.

S3.31.needs: the AGI desktop app on a paid plan, a phone with AGI Mobile signed in to the same account, phone camera for the QR code
S3.31.note: The section returns nothing outside the desktop host and shows a paid-plan notice on Free; the owner memory says Remote Control is hidden in v1, and I did not find a v1 hide flag in this section. Account binding was not traced past the dispatcher (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:2659).
steps: In the AGI desktop app, open Settings and choose Capabilities.
Scroll to the Remote Control section (the section is hidden in a browser and on a Free plan).
Click Pair a phone. A pairing QR code and a short pairing code appear.
On the phone, open AGI Mobile, go to AGI Code, choose Add device, and scan the QR code (or type the pairing code).

Look at the section: it should show the phone as connected (Connected to <phone name>) with a Disconnect phone button, and the pairing should be tied to the same signed-in account. Compare with Expected.
S3.31.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control > Pair a phone (desktop app only, paid plan)

labels.text: Get notified when the response is ready.

S3.32.needs: none (a request long enough that the answer is still generating; the banner does not show again once the browser permission is decided or the banner was dismissed)
S3.32.note: The banner shows only while browser permission is still 'default' and the banner was not resolved before (stored in localStorage), so a tester who already answered once will not see it again; the banner's position in the chat layout was not confirmed.
steps: Sign in and start a new chat.
Send a request that takes a while (for example a long answer or an agent work task).
While the response is still generating, look for the banner 'Get notified when the response is ready.' under the top bar of the chat.
Click Enable to get the browser permission prompt, or click the X labelled 'Dismiss notification prompt' to hide it.
Open Settings > Notifications and find Browser notifications to turn it on or off. Compare with Expected: the offer is optional and can be declined and changed later.
S3.32.where: Chat > long-running answer > banner 'Get notified when the response is ready.' > Enable (or the X to dismiss). To change later: Settings > Notifications > Browser notifications

S3.35.needs: a brand-new account that has never finished onboarding
S3.35.note: The wizard is the /welcome page (apps/web/app/welcome/page.tsx); the code that sends a new account to /welcome after sign-in was not found by grep, so the entry path is unconfirmed. Items S3.33 and S3.34 do not exist in the plan file and were skipped.
steps: Sign in with a brand-new account that has not finished onboarding.
On the screen 'What should we call you?', type a name in Preferred name and click Continue.
On 'What do you want to do first?', read the line 'We will suggest a few prompts to get you started.' and the prompts under 'Start with one of these'.
Click one prompt. The app opens a chat with that prompt placed in the message box (it is filled in, not sent).
Look at the chat: it should show the starter prompt ready to send, leading into a first conversation. Compare with Expected. Clicking Skip for now instead opens the chat without a prompt.
S3.35.where: Sign in with a new account > welcome screen 'What should we call you?' > Continue > 'What do you want to do first?' > a prompt under 'Start with one of these' (or Skip for now)
